q7.answer: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__. Each call (charge, send email, geocode) calls secrets.get("<name>") on the in-memory SecretProvider. The refresh timer swaps in the new value by replacing the object reference under a lock, so the next request uses the new key. A request already in progress keeps the key it read. Module-level client singletons stay, because they hold no key.

q8.answer: Each of the 4 pods reports its current version id for each secret on /healthz. The team compares these with the version ids recorded when the new keys were written in step 2. The team also waits at least 10 minutes (two refresh intervals) after the last old pod stops, then checks each provider console to confirm the old key has had no use since. Any unexplained use blocks revocation. Confirmation rests on reported version ids, not elapsed time.

q9.answer: 1) Set store access and policies, with negative checks. 2) The security on-call creates new keys at the providers (old ones stay active) and writes them to the store. 3) Merge the code PR. It reads from the store and removes the api_key lines from config/app.yaml in the same PR, and adds the CI guard. 4) Preflight read job in prod, then a rolling deploy with a canary hold. 5) Confirm every pod is on the new versions, then revoke the old keys at the providers one at a time. Provider rotation happens first, as creating the new keys, and old-key revocation comes last. Removing keys from the file happens in the same PR as switching the app, not as a separate step. Git history is not rewritten.

q10.answer: The engineer's `make run` sets APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* from the store, using the engineer's own identity. Those paths hold provider sandbox keys, so no prod secrets are read. The path prefix is built from APP_ENV, so there is no prod fallback. Engineers are also denied prod reads by policy. `make run-offline` uses in-memory fake keys and fake provider stubs, and is allowed only when APP_ENV=local.

q11.answer: I never decided this explicitly. By implication it exits non-zero. Startup needs all three keys, and any failed read triggers 3 retries 2 seconds apart, so a missing secret is treated like an unreachable store. The app does not report ready. The plan does not say whether a not-found error should skip the retries and fail fast. Retrying a permanent missing-secret error is the default reading, and I did not distinguish the two.
